change: Authorization security considerations and security best-practices page
rationale: Entry: "Clarify security considerations and best practices in the authorization spec and in a new security best practices page". It adopts, profiles, tightens, or removes no OAuth mechanism; it is security guidance, which the codebook puts in OTHER. Consistent with 2025-11-25#13 (security best-practices update, OTHER in both codings).

Entry: "Add title field for human-friendly display names, so that name can be used as a programmatic identifier". PR #663 gives the motivation as "UI-friendly naming" and "how data is surfaced to end users": UI metadata, coded OTHER like icons (2025-11-25#2, 0.2-0.3#6). The naming separation (DP5) is the secondary code. (First drafted as coder2; reverted on review 2026-11-09 after reading the PR.)

Entry: "Clarify that servers must respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden for invalid Origin headers". Origin validation already existed; the change fixes the error response (DP5: tightens errors, normative definitions). The entry states no security rationale.

change: Tasks moved to io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension; tasks/update
rationale: Entry leads with "Move experimental tasks out of the core protocol and into an official extension"; "moves features to extensions" is the first DP5 criterion, so DP5 is primary and DP3 secondary. The plane stays P2: the redesign changes how long-running work is tracked (polling via tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/list removed), consistent with the worked example 2025-11-25#9 (tasks, P2).

Entry: "Define an error code allocation policy partitioning the JSON-RPC server-error range ... reserved for the MCP specification". It changes who may allocate codes and reserves space for future revisions (P6), unlike 2026-07-28#15, which changes one code's meaning (P4).

Plane = what the change modifies. Removals are coded at the plane of the removed feature in both codings (2025-06-18#1 batching P1, 2026-07-28#5 ping/logging P2); deprecations are coded the same way. The deprecation policy itself is 2026-07-28#27 (P6). Roots, Sampling, Logging are primitives (P4).
As 2026-07-28#22: the deprecated feature is a transport (P1).
As 2026-07-28#22: the deprecated values belong to the sampling primitive (P4).
The correction concerns the type of minimum/maximum/default fields in primitive schemas; schema restructurings are P4 in both codings (2025-11-25#20, 1.0#9). Coder 2 named P4 as the alternative.

Entry: "Add optional referenceTaskIds for task followups". Linking a new task to earlier ones is a richer task primitive; it does not add or change support for long-running work (durability, progress, push notifications, deferred results). The plane definition lists A2A tasks under P4.

change: 0.3.0: mTLS security scheme, OAuth 2.0 metadata URL, per-skill security (breaking)
rationale: Entry: "Add mTLS to SecuritySchemes, add oauth2 metadata url field, allow Skills to specify Security". Two of the three edits (mTLS scheme, per-skill security) are security mechanisms outside the OAuth family; the OAuth metadata URL becomes the secondary code.
The plane definition lists "signed metadata" under P5 verbatim.

Guide: "HTTP+JSON error responses have been updated to use the ProtoJSON representation of google.rpc.Status instead of RFC 9457". The change is the error representation in a binding (P1), unlike the error taxonomy (1.0#5, P4).

change: Agent Card signatures specified with JCS canonicalization and verification rules (signatures added in 0.3)
rationale: Guide: "Canonicalization (RFC 8785) clarified for Agent Card signature"; "Leverage formal specification standards (RFC 8785, RFC 7515)". The signatures existed since 0.3 (0.2-0.3#13); 1.0 specifies them normatively (DP5). Signed metadata is P5 (see 0.2-0.3#13).
Pagination changes the request/response semantics of the list operation (P4); it does not change whether interactions are stateful or how work is tracked.
A new operation for tracking tasks: "how long-running work is tracked" is P2, consistent with the worked example 2025-11-25#9 (tasks, P2). Coder 2 named P2 as the alternative.

Guide: "Multiple concurrent streams allowed; all receive same ordered events"; "Multiple concurrent subscriptions supported per task". The change concerns observing a long-running task (DP3); it neither removes session state nor supports scale-out. DP1 kept as secondary.

The field orders artifact updates streamed for a running task (P2: streaming). No codebook rule decides the pressure; coder 2 marked low confidence and named P2 as the plane alternative, so the first code is kept.

change: Push-notification config operations renamed, flattened, authentication enhanced
rationale: Guide: operations "RENAMED", "TaskPushNotificationConfig flattened", payloads "now use StreamResponse format". The edits are renaming and schema flattening (DP5), as for the other 1.0 renamings (1.0#10, DP5/P4); push notifications (DP3) become the secondary code.
